title: Secants, Tangents and Their Properties
summary: A line that cuts a circle in two points is a secant. A line that touches a circle at exactly one point (the point of contact) is a tangent; it is the limiting position of a secant when the two points of intersection come together. From a point inside a circle no tangent can be drawn; from a point on the circle exactly one; from a point outside exactly two.

(1) A tangent is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact: ∠OPT = 90°. So with OP = radius r, distance OT = d and tangent length t, t² = d² − r² (e.g. OA = 25, tangent 24 ⇒ r = 7).
(2) The two tangents from an external point are equal: PA = PB. They are equally inclined to the line joining the point to the centre, OP bisects ∠APB, and OP is perpendicular to the chord of contact AB.
(3) If tangents PA, PB make angle ∠APB, then ∠AOB = 180° − ∠APB (OAPB has two right angles).
(4) The tangents at the ends of a diameter are parallel.
## Proof: tangents from an external point are equal

Let PA and PB be tangents from P to a circle with centre O. Join OA, OB and OP. In △OAP and △OBP: OA = OB (radii), OP = OP (common), ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (tangent ⊥ radius). So △OAP ≅ △OBP (RHS), and PA = PB (CPCT). Also ∠OPA = ∠OPB.
If two chords AB and CD meet at P (inside or outside the circle), PA × PB = PC × PD. If PAB is a secant and PT a tangent, PA × PB = PT². Example: PA = 4, AB = 5 ⇒ PB = 9, PT² = 36, PT = 6.

The angle between a tangent and a chord through the point of contact equals the angle in the alternate segment. If PT is a tangent at P and PQ a chord, ∠QPT = angle subtended by PQ in the other segment = ½∠POQ. Its converse: a line making such equal angles with a chord is a tangent.

Two circles that do not meet and lie outside each other have 4 common tangents; touching externally — 3; intersecting at two points — 2; touching internally — 1; one inside the other without touching — 0. For a quadrilateral or triangle drawn round a circle (incircle), the tangent lengths from each vertex are equal, so in △ABC with incircle touching BC, CA, AB at D, E, F: AF + BD + CE = AE + CD + BF = ½ perimeter.
mcq: The number of tangents that can be drawn to a circle from a point inside it is —

mcq.work: Every line through an interior point cuts the circle in two points, so it is a secant. No tangent is possible: 0.

mcq: From an external point P, secants PAB and PCD are drawn. If PA = 4 cm, AB = 6 cm and PD = 8 cm, then PC is —

mcq.work:
PB = PA + AB = 10.
PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ 4 × 10 = PC × 8 ⇒ PC = 5 cm.

mcq: A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle with centre O. If ∠AOB = 125°, then ∠COD is —

mcq.work:
For a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle, the angles subtended at the centre by opposite sides are supplementary: ∠AOB + ∠COD = 180°.
∠COD = 180° − 125° = 55°.

mcq: The number of common tangents to two circles that do not touch and lie outside each other is —

mcq.work: Two separate circles have 2 direct and 2 transverse common tangents: 4.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) PT is a tangent at P to a circle with centre O and ∠QPT = 60° (PQ a chord); ∠POQ = ____. (ii) TP and TQ are tangents and ∠POQ = 110°; ∠PTQ = ____.

(i) ∠OPT = 90°, so ∠OPQ = 30° = ∠OQP; ∠POQ = 180° − 60° = 120°. (The central angle is twice the tangent-chord angle.)
(ii) ∠PTQ = 360° − 90° − 90° − 110° = 70°.
Fill in the blanks: (i) PAB is a secant and PT a tangent; PT = x cm, PA = 4 cm, AB = 5 cm, so x = ____. (ii) AB is a diameter, XPY a tangent at P and ∠PBA = 30°; ∠BPY = ____.

(i) PB = 4 + 5 = 9; PT² = PA × PB = 36 ⇒ x = 6.
(ii) ∠BPY equals the angle in the alternate segment, ∠BAP. In △APB, ∠APB = 90° (semicircle), so ∠BAP = 180° − 90° − 30° = 60°. ∠BPY = 60°.
Fill in the blanks: (i) PA and PB are tangents from P; the angle between OP and the chord AB is ____. (ii) X and Y are the points of contact of tangents from P with ∠XPY = 80°; ∠POX = ____.

(i) OP is the perpendicular bisector of the chord of contact AB, so the angle is 90°.
(ii) OP bisects ∠XPY ⇒ ∠OPX = 40°; ∠OXP = 90° ⇒ ∠POX = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°.
Fill in the blanks: (i) PT = 6 cm, AB = 5 cm, PA = x (PAB a secant); x = ____. (ii) PQ is a tangent at Q, QOR a diameter and ∠POR = 120°; ∠OPQ = ____.
Fill in the blanks: (i) Chords AB and CD meet at P; PA = 4, PB = x + 3, PD = 3, PC = x + 5; x = ____. (ii) AB is a diameter, XBY a tangent at B and AC = BC; ∠CBY = ____.

(i) PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ 4(x + 3) = 3(x + 5) ⇒ 4x + 12 = 3x + 15 ⇒ x = 3.
(ii) ∠ACB = 90° and AC = BC, so ∠CAB = 45°. By the alternate segment theorem ∠CBY = ∠CAB = 45°.

Fill in the blanks (any two): (i) Common tangents to two non-intersecting circles ____ (ii) Tangents at a point on the circle ____ (iii) Tangents at the ends of a diameter are ____ (iv) Common tangents to two intersecting circles ____.
(i) 4. (ii) one. (iii) parallel (both are perpendicular to the same diameter). (iv) 2.

case.passage: The London Eye is a giant wheel shaped like a circle with centre O. From a point P on the ground, two straight cables PQ and PR touch the wheel at Q and R, and ∠QPR = 30°. S is a point on the major arc QR.

items.work: PQ = PR (tangents from P), so △PQR is isosceles: ∠RQP = (180° − 30°)/2 = 75°.
∠RSQ = ½∠ROQ = 75° (also equal to ∠RQP by the alternate segment theorem).
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius: ∠ORP = 90°.

vsa: The incircle of △ABC touches BC, CA and AB at D, E and F. Prove that AF + BD + CE = ½(perimeter of △ABC).

Tangents from a point are equal: AF = AE, BD = BF, CE = CD.
Perimeter = AB + BC + CA = (AF + BF) + (BD + CD) + (CE + AE)
= (AF + AE) + (BD + BF) + (CE + CD) = 2AF + 2BD + 2CE.
So AF + BD + CE = ½ × perimeter.

ABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC, and XAY is the tangent at A to its circumcircle. Show that XY ∥ BC.

By the alternate segment theorem, ∠XAB = ∠ACB.
AB = AC ⇒ ∠ABC = ∠ACB. So ∠XAB = ∠ABC.
These are alternate angles made by AB with XY and BC, so XY ∥ BC.

Two tangents PM and PN are drawn to a circle of radius 24 cm from a point P 25 cm from the centre. Find their lengths.

∠OMP = 90°: PM² = OP² − OM² = 625 − 576 = 49 ⇒ PM = 7 cm.

PA and PB are tangents to a circle with PA = 14 cm. A third tangent CD touches the circle at E, with C on PA and D on PB. Find the perimeter of △PCD.

CE = CA and DE = DB (tangents from C and from D).
Perimeter = PC + CD + PD = PC + CE + ED + PD = (PC + CA) + (DB + PD) = PA + PB = 14 + 14 = 28 cm.

Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle.

The chord touches the small circle, so the radius 3 cm is perpendicular to it at its midpoint.
Half-chord = √(5² − 3²) = √16 = 4 cm. Chord = 8 cm.
April 2022
Chords BA and DC of a circle meet, when produced, at P outside the circle. If PA = 4 cm, PB = 10 cm and PC = 5 cm, find CD.

PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ 4 × 10 = 5 × PD ⇒ PD = 8 cm.
CD = PD − PC = 8 − 5 = 3 cm.

sa: Prove that the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are of equal length.

Given: PA and PB are tangents from an external point P to a circle with centre O.
To prove: PA = PB.
Construction: join OA, OB and OP.
Proof: in △OAP and △OBP,
OA = OB (radii);
OP = OP (common);
∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact).
So △OAP ≅ △OBP (RHS), and PA = PB (corresponding parts). Proved.
Chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at P inside the circle. If PA = (3x + 2) cm, PB = (3x − 2) cm, PC = 5⅓ cm and PD = 6 cm, find x.

PA × PB = PC × PD ⇒ (3x + 2)(3x − 2) = (16/3) × 6 = 32.
9x² − 4 = 32 ⇒ 9x² = 36 ⇒ x = 2 (x must be positive).
The angle between radii OA and OB of a circle is 130°. The tangents at A and B meet at T. Find ∠ATB and ∠ATO.
Chords AB and CD of a circle meet at P. If AP = x + 1, BP = x + 2, CP = x and DP = x + 4, find x.
la: SAT is the tangent at A to the circumcircle of △ABC. A line parallel to SAT cuts AB and AC at D and E. Prove that AB × AD = AC × AE.

By the alternate segment theorem, ∠SAB = ∠ACB.
DE ∥ SAT, and AB is a transversal, so ∠ADE = ∠SAB (alternate angles).
Hence ∠ADE = ∠ACB.
In △ADE and △ACB: ∠ADE = ∠ACB and ∠DAE = ∠CAB (common).
So △ADE ~ △ACB (AA), giving AD/AC = AE/AB.
Cross-multiplying: AB × AD = AC × AE. Proved.
PT is a tangent to a circle from an external point P. Chord AB, produced, meets TP at P. TA and TB are joined and TM bisects ∠ATB (M on AB). If ∠PAT = 40° and ∠ATB = 60°, show that PM = PT.

By the alternate segment theorem, ∠PTB = ∠TAB = 40°.
TM bisects ∠ATB, so ∠ATM = ∠MTB = 30°.
∠PTM = ∠PTB + ∠BTM = 40° + 30° = 70°.
∠PMT is an exterior angle of △ATM: ∠PMT = ∠TAM + ∠ATM = 40° + 30° = 70°.
In △PTM, ∠PTM = ∠PMT, so PM = PT. Proved.
Prove that a tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

Given: a circle with centre O and a tangent XY touching it at P.
To prove: OP ⊥ XY.
Proof: take any point Q on XY other than P. Q lies outside the circle (a tangent meets the circle only at P), so OQ > OP (radius).
This is true for every point Q of XY, so OP is the shortest distance from O to XY.
The shortest segment from a point to a line is the perpendicular, so OP ⊥ XY. Proved.
